identification.summary: Storm-1852 is a China-affiliated influence-operations actor described in secondary coverage of Microsoft's October 2024 election reporting; it ran social media accounts posing as right-leaning Trump supporters and left-leaning Americans opposed to Trump, and pivoted to short-form video [S2]. The mapping of Storm-1852 to the name 'Yulong Flood' could not be verified in this check and is unconfirmed.
identification.notes: Earliest dated public mention found is Microsoft's autumn 2024 election reporting as summarized in [S2]; no earlier first-observed date found. The name 'Yulong Flood' was not found in any verified web source. Do not merge with Taizi Flood (Spamouflage), a separate Microsoft-tracked China influence actor tied to MPS-linked activity [S4].

attribution.confidence: Secondary coverage describes Storm-1852 as China-affiliated [S2]. No source found names a specific PRC organization for Storm-1852, unlike Taizi Flood, which coverage ties to the Ministry of Public Security [S4].
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Analysis Center election reporting as summarized by China Digital Times; the primary Microsoft report was not opened [S2].

objectives: Per secondary coverage, the actor did not appear to support one US candidate; it built audiences and amplified conspiracy theories and divisive political content, with videos targeting politicians of both parties [S2]. Underlying strategic intent is not stated in sources found.

sectors: US general public / social media audiences
targeting.notes: Targeting is of US voters and political conversation, not networks; no cyber intrusion activity is attributed to this actor in sources found [S2].

capabilities.summary: Secondary coverage of Microsoft's 2024 reporting says Storm-1852 operated personas posing as right-leaning Trump supporters and left-leaning Americans opposed to Trump, pivoted to short-form video, built audience by replying to comments and live reposting real users' content on breaking news, and after the July 2024 attempt on Trump reposted influencer content alleging Democratic involvement and released original short videos edited from news footage hours later [S2]. Some assets reportedly disappeared after public reporting [S2].

campaigns.name: US election short-form video and persona activity
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's 2024 election reporting, as summarized by China Digital Times, describes Storm-1852 running left- and right-leaning US personas and short-form video targeting politicians of both parties, without clearly favoring one candidate [S2]. Exact report date not verified.

diamond.adversary: China-affiliated influence actor tracked by Microsoft as Storm-1852 (possible alias Yulong Flood, unverified); sponsoring organization not stated in sources found [S2].
diamond.capability: Social media persona networks, short-form video, rapid reaction to news events [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Social media accounts and platforms; no technical infrastructure indicators found in sources.
diamond.victim: US voters and online political audiences during the 2024 election cycle [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: US election-period political discourse and polarization; the actor did not appear to back one candidate [S2].
diamond.technology: Commercial social media and short-form video platforms [S2].

gaps: Primary Microsoft MTAC election reports could not be opened; Storm-1852 details rest on secondary coverage [S2].
The Storm-1852 to 'Yulong Flood' mapping is unverified; sources for it were removed.
Sponsor, unit, or contractor behind the actor is not stated in sources found.
First-observed date, activity after late 2024, platforms, scale, and engagement are unverified.
Relationship to Taizi Flood (Spamouflage) is not established; coverage only contrasts them [S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The relevant environment is the US-facing information environment: social media and short-form video platforms, not DoD networks [S2]. STEP 2: The actor adapts quickly to news events and personas can be removed after public reporting [S2]. STEP 3: Pattern is persona creation posing as US voters, audience-building, and rapid video reaction to events [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued event-driven persona content on US political issues. MDCOA is the same infrastructure redirected at military or crisis events to amplify divisive narratives about US forces. Candidate indicators: newly created accounts posing as service-adjacent or conservative voters, near-simultaneous short videos after a major event. Evidence for DoD-specific targeting is absent from sources found.
